entries.proposition: DESIGN: preterm fetal sheep at 0.7 gestation, 25-minute cord occlusion, then saline or the non-selective alpha antagonist phentolamine (10 mg bolus, 10 mg/h) from 15 minutes to 8 hours; recordings for 72 hours; 18 sham, 18 occluded with saline, 6 with phentolamine.
entries.snippet: Fetuses either received a continuous intravenous infusion of saline or the non‐selective alpha‐adrenergic antagonist phentolamine (10 mg loading bolus, followed by continuous infusion at 10 mg h−1) from 15 min to 8 h post‐HI.

entries.proposition: GROUPING: the groups are described as randomised, but the sex counts place the six phentolamine fetuses in the validation dataset while the pharmacology comparisons use the primary-dataset saline and sham fetuses (8 each); whether phentolamine fetuses were run concurrently with those controls is not stated.
entries.snippet: validation dataset – Sham‐HI 6:4 and HI‐saline 6:4, HI‐phentolamine 4:2

entries.proposition: GLUCOSE AND LACTATE: after the insult glucose and lactate were higher in saline-treated fetuses and recovered by 2 hours with phentolamine, a direct measurement of an alpha-adrenergic contribution to post-insult glycaemia and lactate in a developing-brain model; Table 1 flags glucose differences only at 2 and 4 hours although the text says until 6 hours.
entries.snippet: Glucose and lactate concentrations were higher in the HI‐saline group than the sham‐HI group until 6 h post‐HI but recovered to baseline levels by 2 h in the HI‐phentolamine group (Table 1).
entries.anchor: Results, Cardiovascular and biochemical parameters during HI

entries.proposition: SEIZURES: alpha blockade did not change seizure onset, time with seizures, burden, amplitude, duration or count; the onset means differ (13.3 against 7.3 h) with wide spread.
entries.snippet: There was no difference between the occlusion groups in the average onset time (HI‐saline 13.3 ± 9.2 h; HI‐phentolamine 7.3 ± 2.4 h)
entries.anchor: Results, Post-occlusion neurophysiological and EMG recovery

entries.proposition: UNIT SLIP: the seizure burden is given as seizures per hour (172.4 and 146.1); with a mean duration of about 94 s and 59 seizures over 30 h, 172 seizures per hour is impossible and the figure matches roughly 59 x 94 s / 30 h, about 180 seconds of seizure per hour.
entries.snippet: average seizure burden (HI‐saline 172.4 ± 36.8 seizures h−1; HI‐phentolamine 146.1 ± 47.9 seizures h−1)
entries.anchor: Results, Post-occlusion neurophysiological and EMG recovery

entries.proposition: NO INJURY OUTCOME HERE: the harmful effect of alpha blockade (faster secondary mitochondrial failure, more severe neural injury) is cited from the group earlier study in the same paradigm; this paper reports no histology or injury grade, so it cannot show whether blockade helps or harms.
entries.snippet: phentolamine infusion following HI accelerates the progression of secondary mitochondrial failure and is associated with a more severe neural injury (Dhillon et al., 2023)

entries.proposition: The authors state sympathetic activation is part of an endogenous neuroinhibition after hypoxia-ischaemia that is neuroprotective, the opposite sign to the blockade-benefit reading of the adult mouse seizure study in this group of readings.
entries.snippet: sympathetic nervous system activation and is neuroprotective

entries.proposition: SPECIFICITY OF THE DRUG: phentolamine blocks alpha receptors non-selectively, so subtype contributions are not separated.
entries.snippet: Phentolamine is a non‐specific alpha‐adrenergic receptor antagonist, and so the present study did not investigate the relative contribution of adrenoreceptor subtypes.

entries.proposition: BIOMARKER CLAIM: a threshold one standard deviation above the baseline coefficient of variation, set in the primary group and applied by a blinded observer to a 10 plus 10 validation group, is reported as 90 percent sensitivity and 80 percent specificity; the marker is validated against exposure to the insult, not against measured injury.
entries.snippet: Applying this set threshold, in the validation dataset animals with severe HI were identified with 90% sensitivity and 80% specificity (Fig. 10).
entries.anchor: Results, Viability of short BPV as a biomarker for severe HI

entries.proposition: Figure 10 enlarged: of 10 occluded fetuses, 8 lie above the dashed threshold at about 0.043 and 2 below; of 10 sham fetuses, 1 lies above and 9 below; this gives sensitivity 8 of 10 (95 percent exact interval 44 to 97 percent) and specificity 9 of 10 (55 to 99.7 percent), not 90 and 80 percent as reported.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 10 scatter of 3-hourly systolic CoV: Sham-HI ten black dots with one at about 0.047 above the dashed line near 0.043 and nine at 0.01 to 0.024; HI-Saline ten red triangles with eight between 0.049 and 0.168 and two at about 0.023 and 0.029 below the line.
entries.anchor: Figure 10 (file g011), native JPEG enlarged three times

experimental_context.treatment: phentolamine 10 mg bolus then 10 mg/h from 15 min to 8 h post occlusion, or saline

entries.proposition: LIMITS: stable preterm fetal sheep, not asphyxiated neonates with cardiorespiratory disturbance and routine vasopressor use, which could change variability.
entries.snippet: The studies were undertaken in stable preterm fetal sheep, whereas transitioning asphyxiated neonates experience significant cardio‐respiratory disturbances
